agreedScope.question: How does a receiving team's play differ on its opening possession versus its later possessions within the same point?
agreedScope.unit: Team possessions within receiving points. Point-start O-line role does not establish unchanged personnel after substitutions.
agreedScope.throwCounts: Keep every actual throw, including centering passes and incomplete attempts. Count attempts ending in goals and turnovers separately; stalls and dropped pulls are not physical throws but may end a possession.
agreedScope.huckTiming: Keep throw 1 separate and examine throws 2–3, 4–6, and 7+ using the original numbering. Do not delete or renumber centering passes.
agreedScope.centeringReview: Review concrete examples; no blanket setup-pass rule or league-wide tactical labels are adopted.
agreedScope.huckOutcomes: Actual catches divided by huck attempts are now compared across first, second, and third-or-later team possessions. Drops are incomplete for this measure and reported separately from drop-credited CPOE.
agreedScope.scoring: Possession goals before another turnover, not eventual point holds. Compare starting locations and retain near-end-zone possessions for scoring.
agreedScope.fieldPosition: Main huck comparison requires a first recorded throwing location at least 40 yards from the attacking goal line, with 30-yard, 50-yard and unrestricted sensitivity checks. Scoring and throw counts retain all locations.
agreedScope.timeouts: Main analysis excludes possessions containing recorded timeouts, without renumbering. A sensitivity check additionally excludes whole points containing timeout or injury markers.
notActive: Average throw distance as an outcome
Forward yards per throw as an outcome
agreedScope.centralHypothesis: Subsequent receiving-team possessions may show more willingness to huck and fewer throws before ending. The study tests the behavior; impatience is a motivating explanation, not a measured variable.

interpretationLimits: Fewer throws means fewer passing actions, not necessarily less elapsed playing time.
A huck may reduce the throws needed to advance, but it can also be followed by more passes or a turnover; the relationship must be measured.
Throws 2–3 and 4–6 describe opportunities among possessions that survived to those throws; they are not automatically comparable initiation stages.
A completed huck and a scored possession are different outcomes.
Use all opening possessions for the scoring baseline, not only opening possessions in points with a later regain.
Starting location, team, opponent, game context and changes in personnel may contribute to differences; observational results cannot identify fatigue or impatience.
Team and league comparisons need uncertainty, game-level dependence and multiple comparisons handled explicitly; team aggregation does not guarantee statistical significance.
The expanded cohort audits zero-throw and period-ending possessions; unknown locations are omitted only from location-restricted or adjusted comparisons.

followUpOptions: Review further concrete opening-pass examples before proposing an automatic setup-pass rule.
Use the team patterns to select film examples; test any resulting explanation on additional data.
agreedScopeAsOf: 2026-11-05; later working-design changes are recorded separately below.

workingDesign2026_11_11.fieldPosition: Use 60+ yards to the attacking goal line and same-team nearby-location matches as the working direction.
workingDesign2026_11_11.setupRule: Count the opening transfer from a pull receiver as setup when identified. Subsequent handler resets, confirmed brick-start first throws, and first throws after turnover recovery with play continuing are attacking throws. Keep direct attacks after the pull. Record uncertain starts separately; do not delete every opening pass.
workingDesign2026_11_11.matchingAnchor: The existing 510-pair feasibility calculation uses the first recorded attempt location. If a post-setup attack-start location is chosen, eligibility and matching must be recalculated at that location; those 510 pairs are not validated for a post-setup analysis.
workingDesign2026_11_11.denominators: Keep the original physical throws and full-possession scoring outcomes available. A future after-setup analysis must account separately for setup failures instead of silently dropping them.
workingDesign2026_11_11.filmFirst: UFA.tv subscription verified; review actual footage before changing the counting rule.
workingDesign2026_11_11.setupTerminology: Opening setup is the transfer from a pull receiver to the thrower who initiates the offense; it need not move toward the middle. Later handler resets are attacking throws once the initial downfield looks have begun. For a confirmed brick start, count the first pass as attacking. On a subsequent possession after a turnover with play continuing, count the first pass as attacking, even if it is a short transfer inward. A direct attack after the pull needs no separate setup exchange.
workingDesign2026_11_11.classificationScope: Film-confirmed A, C and G: setup on throw 1, attack begins on throw 2. Film-confirmed H and I: no setup, attack begins on throw 1. F remains a preliminary immediate-attack example. No league-wide automatic labeling or statistical recalculation has been performed.

brickStartExpectation.workingRule: A confirmed brick restart begins attacking on the first pass; retain an exception or uncertainty flag if film contradicts that reading.
brickStartExpectation.evidenceLimit: Teddy’s “99%” expresses a strong expectation based on playing experience, not a measured prevalence from this sample.

attackStartComparison.pullTransfer: For a confirmed completed opening setup transfer, attacking throw 1 is recorded throw 2; use the location after setup if comparing attacking starts.
attackStartComparison.brickOrTurnover: For a confirmed brick start or a subsequent possession with play continuing after a turnover, attacking throw 1 is recorded throw 1.
attackStartComparison.directPullAttack: Retain the first pass if the pull receiver attacks directly rather than making an opening setup transfer.
attackStartComparison.preserveOutcomes: Keep full-possession goals, turnovers and physical-throw counts available. Setup failures must remain accounted for; do not condition overall scoring on successful setup.

largeFilmReview2026_11_11.request: Gather many games and contrasting openings to refine a setup definition and test whether an event-based rule can replace some manual film review.
largeFilmReview2026_11_11.sampling: Games purposefully selected for team coverage. All validated first-quarter receiving-team possessions in each game retained regardless of hucks or scoring. This is not a random league sample.

developmentAndValidation.procedure: Settle and record the rule using development games, then test it unchanged on the reserved games. Changing the rule after inspecting reserved classifications makes that game development material and requires replacement validation data.

largeFilmReview2026_11_11.classificationStatus: No new human or automatic setup labels added. Film access and timing inspection are not setup classifications.

availability.limitations: The Minnesota–Pittsburgh recording starts partway through Q1. Madison opening-pull footage is incomplete. Two Philadelphia subsequent possessions lack enough timestamp evidence for an estimated window. All remain visible and may be marked unclear rather than forced into a category.

largeFilmReview2026_11_11.timingMethod: Each recording was opened through the subscribed UFA.tv player. Selected paused frames and available transcripts were used for approximate sequence anchors. Most case windows are derived from operator timestamps, with 60 seconds of lead-in and 35 seconds afterward. Match score and players; this is not 173 independently watched clips.

spotChecks.observation: Score Philadelphia 1–Carolina 2 at Q1 8:11 aligns with the point-four subsequent-possession sequence; not a setup classification.
Late-Q1 pull near video 29:09 precedes the recorded first-throw huck in point ten. Additional lead-in retained to allow identification of the start.

largeFilmReview2026_11_11.easierRoute: Use event data to locate initial/subsequent possessions and candidate contexts. Derive a simple rule only after film review, then assess agreement, errors, and unclassifiable cases on separate games. Current exports do not directly encode setup, caught-pull status, or downfield looks; short-pass geometry alone is insufficient.
